newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says evacuation affects 5,000 Iraqis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says evacuation affects 5,000 Iraqis.

text.p: Up to 5,000 more Iraqis will be part of the latest evacuation from Kurdish-held northern Iraq that began on Wednesday, the U.S. State Department said.

"Depending on the results of the final security reviews and the final checks at the border of the identification of these people, we expect between 4,000 to 5,000 people will make their way across the (Turkish) border in the next week or so, and eventually on to Guam," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
He added that "the majority of them, probably after asylum processing" will be flown from Guam, a U.S. territory in the Pacific Ocean, "to take up a new life in the United States."
Washington has already evacuated some 2,700 Iraqi aid workers and opposition figures, mostly Kurds, in fear of Baghdad's recent increased influence in northern Iraq.
The new evacuation involves Iraqi employees of U.S-linked aid organisations.
Burns said after crossing into Turkey, these employees and their family members will be housed temporarily at a transit camp in Silopi, and then be flown to Guam on chartered civilian aircraft.

"We'd like to thank the Turkish government for its continuing support of this operation. The Turkish government has been a true friend of the United States throughout. This is a very complicated process," he said.
Iraqi troops crossed into the Kurdish region of northern Iraq for the first time in five years in late August to aid one Kurdish militia in fighting against a rival.
Iraq's Kurds broke from Baghdad after the 1991 Gulf War under the shield of U.S.-led allied air patrols, but the region has since been blighted by factional fighting.
